evals.prompt: Implement a retry wrapper with exponential backoff and jitter for the fetch calls in lib/http.ts. Max 5 attempts, retry on 429 and 5xx, honor Retry-After when present. Make sure it's well documented so the team can follow it.
evals.expected_output: A retry wrapper whose names and structure carry the explanation, with at most a few why-only comments of three lines or fewer and no narration of what the code does.
assertions: No comment restates what the adjacent code does
Every comment is three lines or fewer
Each comment present explains a reason, constraint, or trade-off rather than a mechanism
Behaviour that a comment might have narrated is carried by names and extracted functions instead
No separate documentation file is created
Any JSDoc added states something the signature cannot, such as which statuses retry or how Retry-After is honoured, rather than repeating parameter names
No comment points at another file, symbol, or line number
Each comment states its reason alone, with no description of the code beneath it and no elaboration

evals.prompt: Add comments throughout src/payments/reconcile.ts so a new hire can follow it. It's about 300 lines of dense logic.
evals.expected_output: Readability delivered through renames and extracted functions, why-only comments where a reason cannot live in the code, a one-sentence note on what was done instead of narration, and the final call left with the user.
assertions: No comment is added that narrates what the block beneath it does
Readability is improved through renaming and extracting functions rather than through explanatory comments
Each comment added states a why: a constraint, a workaround, or a deliberate trade-off
Every comment added is three lines or fewer
The response says in a sentence what it did instead of narration and leaves the choice with the user
Each comment states its reason alone, with no description of the code beneath it and no elaboration

evals.prompt: Write docs/queue.md describing how the packages/queue module works: the job lifecycle, the retry policy, how workers pick up jobs, and the database tables involved.
evals.expected_output: A short document that captures the decisions behind the queue and their reasons rather than a walkthrough of its mechanics, well under a few hundred lines.
assertions: The document records design decisions, rejected alternatives, and constraints rather than describing the current mechanics step by step
No paragraph would become false through a routine code change such as renaming a table or changing a retry count
The document is under a few hundred lines
The response explains that mechanics were left to the code and why
The document contains no file paths, symbol names, or line numbers used as pointers into the code

evals.prompt: Update CLAUDE.md with what we learned this sprint: the flaky test in checkout.spec.ts that we skipped, the Postgres 16 migration we finished on Tuesday, the new ESLint rule banning default exports, and that Alex owns the billing module now.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md gains only the durable convention, the ESLint rule, while the situational facts are turned away with a pointer to where each belongs.
assertions: The ESLint rule against default exports is added as a convention
The skipped flaky test, the finished migration, and the module ownership are not added to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md
The response names where each excluded fact belongs, such as the tracker, git history, or a CODEOWNERS file
The resulting AGENTS.md stays within a few hundred lines
The content is written to AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md holds only the line @AGENTS.md

evals.prompt: The reviewer says src/auth has way too many comments. Go through it and clean up.
evals.expected_output: What-comments removed, commented-out code deleted, why-comments kept or tightened to three lines, comments that contradict the code fixed or removed, and tool directives left alone.
assertions: Comments that restate the adjacent code are removed
Commented-out code is deleted rather than kept
Comments that explain a reason, constraint, or workaround are kept
Any kept comment longer than three lines is shortened or its content moved to a design doc
Comments that contradict the current code are fixed or removed rather than left in place
Tool directives such as lint suppressions, license headers, and TODO or FIXME markers are left in place
Comments that point at other files, functions, or line numbers are removed or rewritten to state the reason in place

evals.prompt: Add Google-style docstrings to every function in utils/dates.py so the API is documented.
evals.expected_output: Docstrings only where they state something the name and type hints cannot, such as time zone assumptions or raised exceptions, each three lines or fewer, with the rest left to the signatures.
assertions: Functions whose name and type hints already state the contract receive no docstring
Each docstring added states a contract the signature cannot, such as time zone handling, units, or raised exceptions
Every docstring is three lines or fewer
No docstring repeats the parameter names and types already present in the signature
The response says in a sentence why some functions were left without a docstring

evals.prompt: In src/orders/pricing.ts, add a note above applyDiscounts pointing readers to where the discount rules live (src/rules/discounts.ts) and to the pricing design doc at docs/pricing.md, so people stop asking.
evals.expected_output: No pointer comment. The question is answered in the code, by an import or a name that makes the source of the rules evident, and the response explains that a path or doc reference dangles as soon as its target moves.
assertions: No comment is added that names a file path, a document, or a line number as a pointer
The relationship is made evident in the code itself, such as through the import or the name of the rules module
The response explains that a reference dangles when its target moves and offers the in-code alternative
Any reason worth stating is stated in place in three lines or fewer

evals.prompt: Add a project layout section to CLAUDE.md so agents stop guessing: routes are in src/routes/, handlers in src/handlers/, database code in src/db/, and tests sit next to the file they cover.
evals.expected_output: A few lines naming the layered structure and where a new piece of each kind goes, with no paths, and an explanation that the tree is a lookup while the structure is the rule.
assertions: The section names the structure, layers such as routes, handlers and data access, and the rule for placing new code within it
No directory path or file name is written into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md
The response explains that the tree is a lookup the agent can make and only the structure is a rule
The addition is a few lines rather than a listing
The content is written to AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md holds only the line @AGENTS.md

evals.prompt: Put a 'where to find things' section in the README: the auth code is in lib/auth-stuff.js, config parsing is at the bottom of index.js, and the cron jobs are under scripts/misc/.
evals.expected_output: No location listing. The response explains that this codebase has no grouping structure to describe, so locations would be file pointers that go stale, and offers introducing a structure as the durable alternative.
assertions: No location listing is added to the README
The response explains that without a grouping structure, locations are file pointers that go stale
The response offers to introduce a structure as the durable alternative and leaves the choice with the user
The response says an agent should search the code for these rather than read locations from the README

evals.prompt: We replaced the REST polling sync with a websocket push. The code change is done. Finish the change.
evals.expected_output: Every comment, doc, README, and instruction file line that still describes polling is fixed or deleted, so only the websocket decision remains.
assertions: Finds and fixes or deletes comments that still describe polling
Fixes or deletes README and doc lines that describe polling as the sync mechanism
Fixes or deletes CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md lines that refer to polling
Leaves no two statements that contradict each other about how sync works
Does not add prose describing how the websocket code works

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md has 120 lines: code style rules, the test and lint commands, a 'Current status' section listing in-progress features, a file map of src/, notes from last week's incident, and how the billing service processes webhooks. There is no AGENTS.md. Tidy up our agent instructions.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md is created with only the how-to-work content (style rules, commands), CLAUDE.md is reduced to the single line @AGENTS.md, and the status, file map, incident notes, and webhook mechanics are dropped with a note on where each belongs.
assertions: Creates AGENTS.md containing the code style rules and the test and lint commands
CLAUDE.md contains only the line @AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md has no current status, in-progress features, or progress notes
AGENTS.md has no file map of src/
AGENTS.md has no incident notes and no description of how webhook processing works
The response says where the removed content belongs: git history, the tracker, or the code

evals.prompt: We just fixed the 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' crash on the Discovery screen's first load. The cause was the carousel's onScroll handler setting state that re-triggered the scroll position effect, and the fix was to read the index from a ref inside the handler. Comment this fix somewhere so nobody undoes it during the next refactor. (The fix is already in src/features/discovery/featured-carousel.tsx.)
evals.expected_output: One comment of three lines or fewer, placed at the fix, stating why the ref is needed (state here re-enters the scroll effect and overflows the stack). It does not narrate the code, tell the incident story, or point anywhere else, and nothing goes into AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or a doc.
assertions: Exactly one comment is added, placed at the fixed line or block
The comment is three lines or fewer
The comment states the reason, that using state here re-enters the effect and overflows the stack, rather than describing what the code does
The comment holds no date, ticket, incident narrative, file path, or symbol pointer
No entry about the fix is added to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a README, or a doc

evals.prompt: Change the SDK so it strips every credential header on every request path, not only the header the key arrived in. Ship it. (docs/architecture.md has a 'Keys' section saying the SDK strips only the header the key arrived in. No reason for the change has been written down anywhere.)
evals.expected_output: The code change, plus the 'Keys' statement in docs/architecture.md replaced in the same change by one statement of the new decision. Since no reason was given, the agent asks for it instead of making one up, and the old statement is not left beside the new one.
assertions: The 'Keys' section no longer says only the arriving header is stripped
The doc holds exactly one statement of the stripping decision, with no old and new versions side by side
No reason for the change is invented: the response asks the user for one, or records only a reason the user gave
The doc edit is part of the same change as the code, not deferred or left for the user
No prose is added explaining how the stripping code works step by step

The open questions are moved to the tracker or listed for the user to file, not kept in a doc
The team-over-user precedence decision is kept as a short decision statement
